entityDescription:
ItalConsul was established in 1996 to operate in Logistic Support Area as logistics engineering consultant. Its Core Business is mainly based on its capability to perform advanced project and activities of logistics engineering on the following fields:
Defense; Aerospace; Transportation (Railways); Energy; Manufacturing firms.
The main ItalConsul's skills and experiences are related to the Integrated Logistics Support (ILS) and Finite Elements Methods (FEM) and Analysis (FEA) scenario. It involves, starting from a detailed Logistic Support Analysis (LSA), many activities and deliverables, regarding four different engineering fields:
-- ILS Engineering -- Continuous Acquisition Logistic Support (CALS), Maintenance Planning, System Reliability, Maintainability and Testability, FMEA & FMECA, LCC, FTA, LSA, LSAR, Spare parts analysis, PHS&T analysis, Human factor analysis, Integrated Logistic Support Database (ITP) and Maintenance Management Systems (MMS), NATO Codification.
-- Technical Publications Engineering -- Technical manuals (Interactive Electronic Technical Manuals ¡V IETM, Documentation IETD and Publications - IETP) developed according to the most important international standard requirement (AECMA 2000M, S-1000D, MIL-M-38784, etc.) and using mark-up languages as XML, SGML and HTML.
-- Technical Training Engineering -- Training course, theoretical, hands-on, on the job, Computer Based Training and e-learning SCORM Conformant, System simulations.
-- Concurrent Engineering -- Research of Design bugs and preparation of most convenient solution for the customer.
In order to keep its Know-How to eccellent levels, ItalConsul is active in Research & Development, too. Infact Italconsul holds about seventy scientific publications and three national patents, regularly recorded. Moreover it created a software tool, called "RelySoft", which constitutes a revolutionary approach to Reliability Analysis, particularly in the field of mechanics.
ItalConsul is a member of the The Latium Region SME Cluster operating in the Aerospace and Defence scenarios. This Cluster aims the SME to: intercept more easily R&D programs; strengthen marketing strategies; develop more efficiency industrial partnership, interface international cluster operating in similar scenarios.

entityName: CEREMA Cerema (Centre d’études et d’expertise sur les risques, l’environnement, la mobilité et l’aménagement)
entityDescription:
Cerema is the public expert in adapting territories to climate change. It is the only national institution whose governance is shared between the State and local authorities, with over 950 local authority members.
It is located in France and the French overseas territories, with 27 offices and 2,500 employees.
Cerema's expertise is pooled nationwide, and it supports the State and local authorities in the cooperative development, deployment and assessment of public policies and development and transport projects.
With its strong potential for innovation and research, Cerema operates in 6 areas: Expertise & Territorial Engineering, Building, Mobility, Transport Infrastructures, Environment & Risks, Sea & Coast.
Cerema is a public structure under the authority of the French Ministry of Regional Planning and Decentralization and the Ministry of Ecological Transition, Biodiversity, Forestry, the Sea and Fisheries.
Inside Cerema, the satellite applications team promotes the use of satellite data for public policies and develops methodologies based on spatial data to assist local authorities in their climate change adaptation strategies. It proposes integrated tools for sustainable urban planning and the adaptation of cities and territories to climate change. These tools focus on key areas such as managing natural risks, mitigating urban heat islands, promoting vegetation, improving water management, and supporting coastal management.

entityDescription:
Natural Resources Institute Finland is a research and expert organisation, which promotes bioeconomy and sustainable use of natural resources. Finland is Europe's most forested country - 3/4 of its land area is under forest cover. Finland is rich also in other renewable natural resources, such as fresh water, fishes, game and agricultural land. Luke is the main actor in research of natural resources in Finland.

Natural Resources Institute Finland (Luke) started at the beginning of year 2015, when three state research institutes (MTT Agrifood Research Finland, the Finnish Forest Research Institute, the Finnish Game and Fisheries Research Institute, and the statistical services of the Information Centre of the Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry) were merged. 

The task of Luke are defined in the law and statute to promote competitive business activities based on the sustainable use of renewable natural resources, well-being, and the vitality of rural areas. The Natural Resources Institute Finland supports social decision-making and produces statistics related to food and renewable natural resources. Furthermore, the research institute handles tasks related to ensuring the genetic diversity of cultivated crops, livestock and forest trees. The current network of research units covers the whole country. Luke is a governmental research institute, subordinate to the Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry.

entityDescription:
The Lithuanian Energy Institute (LEI) was established in 1956 and became known among the local and international scientific society interested in fundamental research in hydrodynamics, thermal physics, material science, simulation and control of power supply systems, hydrology. In January 1992 the Government of the Republic of Lithuania granted a state science institution status to the Institute, which became independent from the Academy of Sciences.

The LEI is a technical research centre dealing with energy related research in analysis of security of energy supply, development of energy planning methods, fuel cells and hydrogen, renewable energy, thermal physics and fluid mechanics, nuclear safety, structural integrity assessment of components and structures, simulation of complex energy systems. LEI have 280 persons of staff (as of year 2013). Among them there are 11 Dr. Habilitus, 91 Ph.D., 36 researchers with B.Sc. and M.Sc. and 20 Ph.D. Candidates.

Institute has an extensive experience in international projects: H2020 (1 project), FP7 (23 projects), FP6 (14 projects), FP5 (11 projects), Phare, Intelligent Energy Europe (28 projects), COST (15 projects), IAEA (9 projects), Eureka (4 projects), Leonardo da Vinci (1 project), INTERREG III (3 projects), Baltic Sea Region 2007-2013 programme (3 project), South Baltic Cross-border Co-operation Programme 2007-2013 (1 project), Nordic Energy Research Programme (2 projects).

entityDescription:
Consulting and Innovation: 
Cell & Sat associates acquired during their career a strong expertise in the cellular and satellite fields. They have all been employed by telecom operators or equipment manufacturers, and held various responsibilities including system definition, technical development, business planning, sales & marketing or operational deployment of cellular or satellite networking products.
Cell & Sat engineers contribute their deep knowledge of cellular radio systems to assist telecom operators in the technical and economical evaluation of their networks. Recent assignments concerned the impact of new 3G and 4G developments, emerging network architectures including macro cells as well as small cells, and the impact of fast growing IP based services.
A particular focus of the company is the evaluation of new technologies to extend the coverage of telecommunications networks in rural environments. This includes the technical and economical assessment of satellite transmission systems used to replace or complement terrestrial backhaul infrastructure. Other recent activities concerned the design of cost efficient solar energy systems to serve cellular base stations.
Cell & Sat is also assisting satellite operators and manufacturers in their technical assessments, market evaluations or business plan simulation concerning the potential contribution of satellite systems to telecommunication networks. Recent studies included the impact of various broadband satellite technologies, including geostationary as well as low / medium earth orbit, and the analysis of High Throughput Satellites ¿HTS¿ with spot beams in Ku or Ka bands.
Cell & Sat is working in partnership with selected consulting and development partners to broaden its knowledge and experience base. Cell & Sat is familiar with various aspects of the satellite industry, including business modelling, the management of large international projects and the development of complex satellite platforms and associated ground infrastructure. 
Cell & Sat engineers have a particular interest for innovation in the cellular and satellite fields. The company patented and developed innovative functions to reduce the cost and optimize the quality of satellite infrastructure within cellular networks. Its initial developments concerned the optimization of satellite backhaul by locally switching 2G mobile voice channels, while Cell & Sat ongoing research activity is now focussing on the application of satellite technologies to efficiently transport 3G/4G mobile data

entityDescription: EBE Solutions has years of experience in managing R&D projects in the field of road safety and telematics and has successfully undertaken numerous R&D projects over the past years. Many exciting products and services of their portfolio are based on the results of previous R&D projects. For example, EBE developed and implemented a Park & Ride entry/exit control system for the parking garages of the Austrian Federal Railways (ÖBB) to prevent unauthorized persons (no train ticket) from parking illegally. EBE also developed a modern railway crossing safety system and a red light enforcement system at railway crossings. This was very challenging due to competitors in Austria and Germany, as these systems were split between two companies until EBE entered the market. Market entry in the road and rail safety sector is very difficult due to high safety and norm standards and sometimes involves high financial resources. EBE has been involved in the digitalization of roadworks in the road traffic sector for many years. Some time ago, a start was made on connecting roadworks safety components to a control center via a network. This means that information regarding position and display information is supplied to the control center. From this, requirements for simple traffic jam warning systems were defined and developed for use in Europe. EBE Solutions is responsible for project management and organization, as well as the facilitation of project meeting. Project meetings will be held on a regular basis to ensure the information flow between the partners.

entityDescription:
The University of Applied Sciences Upper Austria (FH OÖ) was established in 1994. FH OÖ contains of four campuses in Upper Austria located in the major cities Linz, Steyr, Wels and the important IT-Centre Hagenberg. In total there are about 50 academic study programs in the specific fields of IT, Communication and Media (Hagenberg), Health and Social Sciences (Linz), Business (Steyr) as well as Engineering and Environmental Sciences (Wels). The University has reinforced its research and development activities in recent years by establishing a Research & Development Centre at each Campus. These Research Centres cover 15 main areas of inquiry that reflect the evolving body of knowledge in the 21st century and together constitute Austria's no. 1 University of Applied Sciences in R&D. The main focus is on research that will lead to sophisticated and practical applications for the benefit of commerce and society. FH OÖ comprises about 180 full-time researchers (state: June 2013). As stated in the company register FH OÖ Forschungs & Entwicklungs GmbH is a non-profit-organization and does not generate any profit from its activities.
In 2013 FH OÖ processed over 320 R&D projects with a total turnover of over €13 Mio. For the management of these R&D projects FH OÖ established a 'FH OÖ F&E GmbH' in 2003 as an own legal entity only for R&D activities. Since then all national, European and international R&D projects are handled through a central coordination to easier manage financial and organizational aspects of R&D projects. Furthermore each R&D Centre at the four campuses has an own Research Center head who supports researchers on site.

entityDescription: Nextworks, located in Pisa (Italy), is a very dynamic SME that was created in 2002 by a group of engineers and computer scientists as a spin-off company of the Department of Computer Science and Telecommunications (DITEL) of Consorzio Pisa Ricerche (CPR), in order to exploit the vast experience gained since 1995 in the context of National and International research projects and consultancies. Nextworks operates in the IT and Telecommunications sectors. The company has long-term experience and proved skills in the frameworks of wireless, access and transport networks, digital video encoding and transport, control and automation, design and development of complex software systems on both traditional and embedded platforms. The consulting activities range from pure support consulting to long-term, third-party design & developments of protocol stacks for equipment vendors. Nextworks has been running out research and development activities in co-funded projects (EU, National and Regional). This work is carried out in cooperation with a wide range of partners (both academic and industrial), with the basic objective to consolidate and further develop the know-how of its personnel, designed to provide consulting and training, development of products and the development of their relations on the basis of future consulting and R&D. The technology sector is the reference ICT in general and frontier technologies in particular. Based on the experience gained from its teams, Nextworks promotes the dissemination and use of technologies and services at the border of the area of research and real application contexts, with the following activities: ¿ research and development in the context of emerging technologies and protocols, through the preliminary stages of study, evaluation of applicability, prototyping and product development, designed to turn innovative ideas into successful solutions; ¿ specialized training on specific technical issues, intended for companies that need to establish or strengthen their know-how or to start new industrial activities; ¿ consultancy and technical support in the areas of networking, security, and traditional/innovative services, accompanying its customers both in the early stages of realization and in the evolution and optimization of their IT infrastructure; ¿ Design and development of software and systems on data, voice and video processing and transmission, tailored to customers specific requirements in contexts ranging from home environment to industry; ¿ integration and customization of open source software, particularly in the areas of competence of the company. Since 2004, Nextworks is actively present in the market for home automation in the yachting sector, supporting one of the largest European shipyards in the design, construction and installation of their standard unified IT system, which integrates all of the electronic technologies on board. Since 2008, Nextworks produces two lines of home automation products for high-end yachting and residential markets: SeaLux (www.sealux.it) and Symphony (www.hellosymphony.it). These innovative solutions are fully developed in-house, and are characterized by the integration of home automation, security, communications and multimedia entertainment.

entityDescription:
AYESA has a long record of designing and building data centres. 

It provides levels of security that are capable of guaranteeing uninterrupted operation. It adopts top-level solutions to raise service continuity to the maximum regardless of any failures that may occur. 

It designs and executes shielding under standard EN1047-2, electrical subsystems with a minimum redundancy of 2N in all components from supply to the power source of IT equipment.

It incorporates sustainability criteria, thoroughly analysing power, redundancies, control and energy efficiency. It implements the most modern fire protection systems and secure access control systems. 

It scales the architecture of hardware, networks and software, and efficiently manages the purchase and supply of equipment, including servers, storage and backup systems, high availability software and structured cables
